123.subject: Botany
123.text: People recovering from long illness are often advised to include the alga Spirulina in their diet because it
options: makes the food easy to digest
123.sol: Spirulina is a blue-green algae. Spirulina platensis is one of the richest source of protein, containing 40-50 percent crude protein on dry weight basis which under favourable condition may reach upto 70 percent. Its protein has balanced composition containing all essential amino-acids and lysine and tryptophan being present in sufficient quantities. Spirulina is also rich in vitamins, particularly Vit. $\mathrm{B}_{12}$, which is not common in plant products and contains considerable amounts of fats, carbohydrates and minerals. It's lipids are made up of unsaturated fatty acids that do not form cholesterol.

7003.text: If the chord of contact of tangents from a point \(A\) to a given circle passes through \(B\), then the circle with \(A B\) as a diameter will ____
options: Neither intersect nor touch the given circle
7003.sol:
Let an equation of circle
\(x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0 \text{ and point } A$\left(x_1, y_1\right)\)
Then equation of chord of contact is
\$(\begin{aligned}$ x x_1+y y_1+g\left(x+x_1\right)$+f\left(y+y_1\right) +c & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad$\left(x_1+g\right)$$ x+$\left(y_1+f\right)$ y+\left(g x_1+f y_1+c\right) & =0
\end{aligned}\)
Let another point \(B\left(x_2, y_2\right)\) through which chord (i) passes, so
\(x_1 x_2+g x_2+y_1 y_2+f y_2+g x_1+f y_1+c=0 \quad \ldots (ii)\)
Now equation of circle having \(A B\) as diameter is
\$(\begin{aligned}$& \left(x-x_1\right)\left(x-x_2\right)$+\left(y-y_1\right)\left(y-y_2\right)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x²+y²-\left(x_1+x_2\right)$$ x-$\left(y_1+y_2\right)$$ y +x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2=0 \quad \ldots (iii)
\end{aligned}\)
By the circles
\(x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0 \text{ and circle (iii) }\)
the \(2 g_1 g_2+2 f_1 f_2\)
\$(\begin{aligned}$& =-2 g$\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}\right)-2$$ f$\left(\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)$ \\
& =-g x_1-g x_2-f y_1-f y_2 \\
& =x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2+c \quad \{$\text{from Eq. (ii)}$$\} \\
& =c_1+c_2 \\
\because 2 g_1 g_2 & +2 f_1 f_2=c_1+c_2
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Circles \(x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0\) and Eq. (iii) cuts orthogonally.
Hence, option (b) is correct.

7915.text:
While solving a system of linear equations $\mathrm{AX}=\mathrm{B}$ using Cramer's rule with the usual notation if
$\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right| ; \Delta_1=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ 11 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right|$ and $X=\left[\begin{array}{l}\alpha \\ 2 \\ \beta\end{array}\right]$ then

7915.sol:
Given, $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right| \Rightarrow \Delta_1=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ 11 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right|$ and $x=\left[\begin{array}{l}\alpha \\ 2 \\ \beta\end{array}\right]$

So, $\alpha+2+\beta=5 \Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=3 \ldots(i)$
and, $-\alpha+2+5 \beta=11 \Rightarrow-\alpha+5 \beta=9 \ldots(ii)$
After solving equations (i) and (ii), we get $\alpha=1, \beta=2$ So, $\alpha^2+\beta^2=1+4=5$

& \text{ I. } \mathrm{F}=e^{\int-\frac{1}{y} d y}=e^{-\log y}=\frac{1}{y}\\

10350.text: The number of numbers between 2000 and 5000 that can be formed with the digits 0,1 , 2, 3, 4 (repetition of digits not allowed) and are multiple of 3 is
10350.sol:
Number between 2000 and 5000 is a 4 digits number.
For the multiples of 3, the sum of digit must be divisible by 3.
There are only 2 ways of selecting the digits so that 4 digit number with the given digits can be formed, i.e. 0, 1, 2, 3 and 0, 2, 3, 4.
The number of ways of forming number with digit $0,1,2,3$ is $2 \times 3$ ! $\quad[\because 0$ and 1 cannot be place on thousand place]
The number of ways of forming number with the digit $0,2,3,4$ is $3 \times 3 ! \quad[\because 0$ cannot be place on thousand digit]
Hence, the required number of ways $\begin{aligned}
& =2 \times 3 !+3 \times 3 ! \\
& =3 !(2+3)=6 \times 5=30
\end{aligned}$

14801.text: A gaseous mixture consists of $4 \mathrm{~g}$ oxygen and $4 \mathrm{~g}$ of helium. The ratio $\frac{C_p}{C_V}$ of mixture is $\left(C_p\right. and C_V$ are molar specific heats of the mixture at constant pressure and at constant volume respectively).
14801.sol:
For a gas mixture,
$r_{\text{mixture }}=\frac{C_{p_{(\mathrm{mix})}}}{C_{V(\text{ mix })}}=\frac{\left(\frac{n_1 C_{p_1}+n_2 C_{p_2}}{n_1+n_2}\right)}{\left(\frac{n_1 C_{V_1}+n_2 C_{V_2}}{n_1+n_2}\right)}\Rightarrow \quad r_{\text{mix }}=\frac{n_1 C_{p_1}+n_2 C_{p_2}}{n_1 C_{V_1}+n_2 C_{V_2}}$  ...(i)

Now, number of moles of oxygen, $n_1=\frac{m}{M}=\frac{\text{ Sample mass }}{\text{ Molar mass }}n_1=\frac{4}{32}=\frac{1}{8}$
Similarly number of moles of helium, $n_2=\frac{4}{4}=1$
Also oxygen is a diatomic gas so,
$C_{p_1}=\frac{7}{2} R$ and $C_{V_1}=\frac{5}{2} R$
Helium is monoatomic, hence
$C_{p_2}=\frac{5}{2} R, C_{V_2}=\frac{3}{2} R$
Substituting these values in eq. (i) we get,
$r_{\text{mix }}=\frac{\frac{1}{8} \times \frac{7}{2} R+1 \times \frac{5}{2} R}{\frac{1}{8} \times \frac{5}{2} R+1 \times \frac{3}{2} R}=\frac{\frac{7}{16}+\frac{5}{2}}{\frac{5}{16}+\frac{3}{2}}
or \quad r_{\text{mix }}=\frac{7+40}{5+24}=\frac{47}{29}$

19836.text: The value of $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}$ for the phosphorylation of glucose in glycolysis is $13.8 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$. The value of $K_{C}$ at $298 \mathrm{ K}$ is
19836.sol:
The relationship between the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}$ and the equilibrium constant $K_{C}$ is given by the equation $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -RT \ln K_{C}$.

Given values are $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = 13.8 \text{ kJ/mol} = 13800 \text{ J/mol}$, $R = 8.314 \text{ J/(mol K)}$, and $T = 298 \text{ K}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$13800 = -(8.314) \times (298) \times \ln K_{C}$

$\ln K_{C} = -\dfrac{13800}{8.314 \times 298}$

$\ln K_{C} = -\dfrac{13800}{2477.572} \approx -5.570$

$K_{C} = e^{-5.570}$

$K_{C} \approx 3.81 \times 10^{-3}$

Answer: $3.81 \times 10^{-3}$

19898.subject: Chemistry
19898.text: The time required for $80 \%$ of a first order reaction is "$y$" times the half-life period of the same reaction. What is the value of "$y$"?
19898.sol:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right).

The half-life period $t_{1/2}$ is given by $t_{1/2} = $\dfrac{0.693}{k}.

For 80\%$ completion, $[A]_t = [A]_0 - 0.80[A]_0 = 0.20[A]_0$.

The time $t_{80\%}$ is $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{0.20[A]_0} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log(5)$.

Using $\log(5) $\approx$0.699$, $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303 \times 0.699}{k} = \dfrac{1.61}{k}.

We are given $ t_{80\%} = y $\times$ t_{1/2}$, so $y = $\dfrac{t_{80\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{1.61/k}{0.693/k} = \dfrac{1.61}{0.693} \approx2.32$.

Answer: 2.32

20216.text:
Match the mixtures listed in Column I with the correct method used for their separation.
Column IColumn II
A. Glycerol from spent LyeP. Steam distillation
B. Mixture of Benzoic acid and Naphthalene dissolved in organic solventQ. Distillation

20216.sol:
Glycerol from spent lye is separated by distillation under reduced pressure because glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point.

A mixture of benzoic acid and naphthalene dissolved in an organic solvent can be separated by differential extraction using aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$. Benzoic acid reacts with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to form a water-soluble salt, while naphthalene remains in the organic layer.

Aniline (boiling point $457 \text{ K}$) and chloroform (boiling point $334 \text{ K}$) have a large difference in their boiling points and can be separated by simple distillation.

2-Nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol are separated by steam distillation. 2-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas 4-nitrophenol is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Thus, the correct matching is A → R, B → S, C → Q, D → P.

Answer: A — R B—S C—Q D—P

20707.text:
When 1 mole of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and 1 mole of ammonia are made to react in the reaction,

$4 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{ g})+5 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$
options: $1.0 \text{ mole$ of NO will be produced }
20707.sol:
The balanced chemical equation is $4 \mathrm{NH}_3(g) + 5 \mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}(g) + 6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(g)$.

Given initial moles are $n(\mathrm{NH}_3) = 1$ mole and $n(\mathrm{O}_2) = 1$ mole.

To find the limiting reagent, calculate the ratio of moles to stoichiometric coefficients:
For $\mathrm{NH}_3: \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$
For $\mathrm{O}_2: \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.20$

Since $0.20 < 0.25$, $\mathrm{O}_2$ is the limiting reagent.

Using the stoichiometry of the reaction, 5 moles of $\mathrm{O}_2$ produce 4 moles of $\mathrm{NO}$ and 6 moles of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

Therefore, 1 mole of $\mathrm{O}_2$ produces:
$n(\mathrm{NO}) = \dfrac{4}{5} \times 1 = 0.8$ moles of $\mathrm{NO}$.
$n(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}) = \dfrac{6}{5} \times 1 = 1.2$ moles of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

Answer: $\text{ Oxygen is the limiting reagent }$

20771.text: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass 6.63 g moving with a velocity of $100 \mathrm{ m} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ is:
20771.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ is given by the formula $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $m$ is the mass of the particle, and $v$ is its velocity.

Given values are:
$h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$
$m = 6.63 \text{ g} = 6.63 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$
$v = 100 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 10^{2} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Substituting these values into the formula:
$\lambda = \dfrac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{(6.63 \times 10^{-3}) \times 10^{2}}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{6.63 \times 10^{-1}}$

$\lambda = 10^{-34 - (-1)} = 10^{-33} \text{ m}$

Answer: $10^{-33} \mathrm{ m}$

21984.subject: Mathematics
21984.text: If S is the sum to infinity of a decreasing geometric progression with common ratio $x$ such that $|x| < 1 ; x \neq 0$. The ratio of fourth term to the second term is $\dfrac{1}{16}$ and the ratio of the third term to the square of the second term is $\dfrac{1}{9}$. Then the value of S is
21984.sol:
Let the first term of the geometric progression be $a$ and the common ratio be $x$. The terms are $a, ax, ax^2, ax^3, \dots$.

Given the ratio of the fourth term to the second term is $\dfrac{1}{16}$, we have $\dfrac{ax^3}{ax} = x^2 = \dfrac{1}{16}$. Since the progression is decreasing and $|x| < 1$, we take $x = \dfrac{1}{4}$ (as $x = -\dfrac{1}{4}$ would lead to an alternating series, but the problem implies a standard decreasing GP).

Given the ratio of the third term to the square of the second term is $\dfrac{1}{9}$, we have $\dfrac{ax^2}{(ax)^2} = \dfrac{ax^2}{a^2x^2} = \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{1}{9}$. Thus, $a = 9$.

The sum to infinity $S$ of a geometric progression is given by $S = \dfrac{a}{1 - x}$.

Substituting the values $a = 9$ and $x = \dfrac{1}{4}$, we get $S = \dfrac{9}{1 - 1/4} = \dfrac{9}{3/4} = 9 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = 12$.

Answer: 12

The given lines are $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_{1} + \lambda \vec{b}_{1}$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_{2} + \mu \vec{b}_{2}$, where $\vec{a}_{1} = 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}_{1} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{a}_{2} = 2\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, and $\vec{b}_{2} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$.

First, check if the lines are parallel. Since $\vec{b}_{1} \times \vec{b}_{2} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \times (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 4 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(8-9) - \hat{j}(4-6) + \hat{k}(3-4) = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k} \neq \vec{0}$, the lines are not parallel.

Next, check if the lines intersect by calculating the scalar triple product $(\vec{a}_{2} - \vec{a}_{1}) \cdot (\vec{b}_{1} \times \vec{b}_{2})$.

$\vec{a}_{2} - \vec{a}_{1} = (2\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) - (2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$.

$(\vec{a}_{2} - \vec{a}_{1}) \cdot (\vec{b}_{1} \times \vec{b}_{2}) = (2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}) \cdot (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}) = (2)(-1) + (4)(2) + (6)(-1) = -2 + 8 - 6 = 0$.

Since the scalar triple product is zero, the lines are coplanar. As they are not parallel, they must be intersecting lines.

Answer: Intersecting lines

22205.subject: Mathematics
22205.text: The line $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-3}{4}=\dfrac{z-4}{5} is parallel to the plane$
22205.sol:
The direction vector of the line $\dfrac{x-2}{3} = \dfrac{y-3}{4} = \dfrac{z-4}{5}$ is $\vec{v} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.

A line is parallel to a plane if its direction vector $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to the normal vector $\vec{n}$ of the plane, which implies the dot product $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{n} = 0$.

Checking the options:

For option (1), the normal vector is $\vec{n} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. The dot product is $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{n} = (3)(3) + (4)(4) + (5)(5) = 9 + 16 + 25 = 50 eq 0$.

For option (2), the normal vector is $\vec{n} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. The dot product is $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{n} = (3)(2) + (4)(3) + (5)(4) = 6 + 12 + 20 = 38 eq 0$.

For option (3), the normal vector is $\vec{n} = 1\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} - 1\hat{k}$. The dot product is $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{n} = (3)(1) + (4)(1) + (5)(-1) = 3 + 4 - 5 = 2 eq 0$.

For option (4), the normal vector is $\vec{n} = 2\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$. The dot product is $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{n} = (3)(2) + (4)(1) + (5)(-2) = 6 + 4 - 10 = 0$.

Since the dot product is zero, the line is parallel to the plane $2x + y - 2z = 0$.

Answer: $2 x+y-2 z=0$

22803.text: A small metallic sphere carrying a charge $2 \times 10^{-6} C$ is suspended using a thin thread of negligible mass from a rigid support, in a horizontal electric filed $5 \times 10^4 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$. If the thread is making an angle $30^0$ with the vertical, What is the tension in the thread?
22803.sol:
Let $q = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$ be the charge on the sphere, $E = 5 \times 10^4 \text{ Vm}^{-1}$ be the electric field, and $\theta = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$ be the angle the thread makes with the vertical.

The forces acting on the sphere are the gravitational force $mg$ acting downwards, the electric force $F_e = qE$ acting horizontally, and the tension $T$ in the thread.

In equilibrium, the forces are balanced:

$T \sin \theta = qE$

$T \cos \theta = mg$

From the first equation, $T = \dfrac{qE}{\sin \theta}$.

Substituting the given values:

$T = \dfrac{(2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}) \times (5 \times 10^4 \text{ Vm}^{-1})}{\sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}}$

$T = \dfrac{10^{-1}}{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$T = 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2 \text{ N}$

Answer: 0.2 N

23561.subject: Physics
23561.text: An ideal gas is expanding such that $P T^2=$ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is
23561.sol:
The equation of state for an ideal gas is $PV = nRT$.

Given $PT^{2} = C$, where $C$ is a constant, we can write $P = C T^{-2}$.

Substituting this into the ideal gas equation, we get $(C T^{-2}) V = nRT$.

Rearranging for $V$, we have $V = \dfrac{nR}{C} T^{3}$.

The coefficient of volume expansion $\gamma$ is defined as $\gamma = \dfrac{1}{V} \left( \dfrac{dV}{dT} \right)_{P}$.

Differentiating $V$ with respect to $T$ from the relation $V = \dfrac{nR}{C} T^{3}$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dT} = 3 \dfrac{nR}{C} T^{2}$.

Substituting $V$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dT}$ into the expression for $\gamma$:

$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{\left( \dfrac{nR}{C} T^{3} \right)} \left( 3 \dfrac{nR}{C} T^{2} \right) = \dfrac{3}{T}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{T}$

26825.text: A hydroxy compound $(\mathrm{X})$ with molar mass $122 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. In acetylation, each hydroxyl group reacts:
R-OH + (CH₃CO)₂O → R-O-CO-CH₃ + CH₃COOH.
Each -OH is converted to -OCOCH₃, resulting in a net mass increase of 42 g/mol per hydroxyl group (addition of acetyl group mass 43, removal of hydrogen mass 1).
Given: Original molar mass = 122 g/mol, Product molar mass = 290 g/mol
Total mass increase = 290 - 122 = 168 g/mol
Number of hydroxyl groups = 168 ÷ 42 = 4

36329.subject: Mathematics
36329.text: Let $A=\{(a,b,c): a,b,c \text{ are non-negative integers and } a+b+2c=22\}$. Then $n(A)$ is equal to:
36329.sol:
The given equation is $a + b + 2c = 22$, where $a, b, c$ are non-negative integers.

This can be rewritten as $a + b = 22 - 2c$.

Since $a \ge 0$ and $b \ge 0$, we must have $22 - 2c \ge 0$, which gives $c \le 11$.

Since $c$ is a non-negative integer, the possible values for $c$ are $0, 1, 2, \dots, 11$.

For a fixed value of $c$, the number of non-negative integer solutions to the equation $a + b = 22 - 2c$ is given by $(22 - 2c) + 1 = 23 - 2c$.

The total number of solutions $n(A)$ is the sum of the number of solutions for each possible value of $c$:

$n(A) = \sum_{c=0}^{11} (23 - 2c)$

$n(A) = 23 + 21 + 19 + \dots + 1$

This is an arithmetic progression with $12$ terms, first term $1$, and last term $23$.

$n(A) = \dfrac{12}{2} (1 + 23) = 6 \times 24 = 144$

Answer: $144$

37458.text: Define a relation $R$ over a class of $n \times n$ real matrices $A$ and $B$ as "$ARB$ iff there exists a non-singular matrix $P$ such that $PA{P}^{- 1} = B$". Then which of the following is true ?
options: $R$ is symmetric, transitive but not reflexive
$R$ is reflexive, symmetric but not transitive
$R$ is reflexive, transitive but not symmetric
37458.sol:
Given $A$ and $B$ are matrices of $n \times n$ order and $ARB$ iff there exists a non-singular matrix $P\left(det \left(P\right) \ne 0\right)$ such that $PA{P}^{- 1} = B$.

Reflexivity Check :

$ARA ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = A$ which is true for $P = I$.

So, $R$ is reflexive relation.

Symmetric Check :

$ARB ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = B ⇒ {P}^{- 1}PA{P}^{- 1}P = {P}^{- 1}BP ⇒ IAI = {P}^{- 1}BP ⇒ {P}^{- 1}BP = A ⇒ BRA$ for matrix ${P}^{- 1}$.

So, $R$ is symmetric relation.

Transitivity Check :

$ARB ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = B$ and $BRC ⇒ PB{P}^{- 1} = C$.

So, $PPA{P}^{- 1}{P}^{- 1} = C$.

$⇒ {P}^{2}A{\left({P}^{2}\right)}^{- 1} = C ⇒ ARC$

So, $R$ is a transitive relation.

Since, $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive all.

Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

37546.text: Let $9 = {x}_{1} < {x}_{2} < \ldots < {x}_{7}$ be in an A.P. with common difference $d$. If the standard deviation of ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2} \ldots , {x}_{7}$ is 4 and the mean is $\overset{¯}{x}$, then $\overset{¯}{x} + {x}_{6}$ is equal to :

$9, 9 + d, 9 + 2d, \ldots \ldots \ldots . 9 + 6d$

Now subtracting $9$ from the series we get,

$0, d, 2d, . . . . . . . 6d$

So, mean will be $\overset{¯}{x}new = \dfrac{21d}{7} = 3d$

Now using the formula of variance we get,

${\sigma}^{2} = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2} - {\left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ d = 2$

38936.subject: Physics
38936.text: The ratio of momentum of the photons of the $1^{st}$ and $2^{nd}$ line of Balmer series of Hydrogen atoms is $\alpha/\beta$. The possible values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are:-
38936.sol:
The momentum of a photon is given by $p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$.

From Rydberg's formula, the wave number is $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$.

For the first line of the Balmer series, the transition is from $n_2 = 3$ to $n_1 = 2$.

$p_1 = \dfrac{h}{\lambda_1} = hR \left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2} \right) = hR \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9} \right) = \dfrac{5hR}{36}$

For the second line of the Balmer series, the transition is from $n_2 = 4$ to $n_1 = 2$.

$p_2 = \dfrac{h}{\lambda_2} = hR \left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{4^2} \right) = hR \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{16} \right) = \dfrac{3hR}{16}$

The ratio of the momenta is:

$\dfrac{p_1}{p_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{5hR}{36}}{\dfrac{3hR}{16}} = \dfrac{5}{36} \times \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{20}{27}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$, the possible values are $\alpha = 20$ and $\beta = 27$.

Answer: $20$ and $27$

For a nucleus $X ZA$ having mass number A and atomic number $Z$

A. The surface energy per nucleon$( {b}_{s} ) = – {a}_{1}A\dfrac{2}{3} .$

The formula to calculate the radius of a nucleus is given by

$R = {R}_{0}A\dfrac{1}{3} . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, the volume energy can be written as

$\begin{cases}{b}_{v} & = & {C}_{1}{R}^{3} \\ & = & {a}_{3}{\left(A\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{3} \\ & = & {a}_{3}A\end{cases}$

The nuclear binding energy is the minimum energy that is required to disassemble the nucleus of an atom into its constituent protons and neutrons. Also, the energy of the nucleus is negative with regard to the energy of the particles pulled apart to infinite distance, because energy must be utilised to split a nucleus into its individual protons and neutrons. It is proportional to the surface area.

Hence, statements C and D are most appropriate.

43427.subject: Physics
43427.text: For the given logic circuit, which of the following inputs combination will make both LED$-1$ and LED$-2$ to glow?
43427.sol:
Let the output of the OR gate be $Y_1$.

$Y_1 = A + B$

For LED-1 to glow, $Y_1$ must be $1$, which means $A + B = 1$.

Let the output of the first AND gate be $Y_2$.

$Y_2 = Y_1 \cdot C = (A + B) \cdot C$

Let the output of the second AND gate be $Y_3$.

$Y_3 = A \cdot Y_2 = A \cdot (A + B) \cdot C$

For LED-2 to glow, $Y_3$ must be $1$.

Simplifying the Boolean expression for $Y_3$:

$Y_3 = (A \cdot A + A \cdot B) \cdot C$

$Y_3 = (A + AB) \cdot C$

$Y_3 = A(1 + B) \cdot C$

$Y_3 = A \cdot C$

For $Y_3 = 1$, we require $A = 1$ and $C = 1$.

If $A = 1$, then $Y_1 = 1 + B = 1$ for any value of $B$, satisfying the condition for LED-1 to glow.

From the given options, the combination $A = 1, B = 0, C = 1$ satisfies these conditions.

Answer: $A = 1, B = 0, C = 1$

44899.sol: Contractile vacuole is the clear rounded, pulsating body present in the posterior part of endoplasm of Amoeba. It is found only in fresh water forms and is mainly concerned with osmoregulation, ie, removal of excess of water. Plasmalemma, a trilaminar and selectively permeable membrane covering the body, functions both in excretion (ammonia) and respiration in Amoeba.Pseudopodia (false feet) are finger-like and blunt-extensions of cell body in protozoans. In Amoeba, the type of pseudopodium found in lobopodium, composed of both ectoplasm and endoplasm. It is temporary locomotory structure which is also meant for feeding in Amoeba. Locomotion of Amoeba is known as'amoeboid movement' (Sol-gel theory).

48329.text: A metal exists as an oxide with formula $M_{0.96} \mathrm{O}$. Metal, $M$ can exist as $M^{2+}$ and $M^{3+}$ in its oxide $M_{0.96} \mathrm{O}$. The percentage of $M^{3+}$ in the oxide is nearly
48329.sol:
We are given metal oxide with formula $M_{0.96} \mathrm{O} . Here, $M$ can exist as $M^{2+}$ as well as $M^{3+}$. Here, for every 100 oxide ions there are $96 M$ ions.
Let out of this $96 M$ atoms, $M^{2+}$ exists $=x and M^{3+}$ will be $=(96-x)$.
Total positive charge on $96 M$-atoms
$=2 \times x+3 \times(96-x)$
Total negative charge on $100 $\mathrm{O}$-atoms $=100 \times 2=200$
As per electrical neutrality concept
 \begin{aligned}
2 x+3(96-x) &=200 \\
2 x+288-3 x &=200 \\
-x &=200-288 \\
-x &=-88 $\text{$ or } x=88 \\
96-88 &=8
\end{aligned}$
So, the ratio of $M^{3+}$ will be  \frac{8}{96}  \times 100=8.3 \%$

51988.sol:
Given trigonometric relation is&

$\left(\dfrac{1}{3}sin\theta + \dfrac{2}{3}cos\theta\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{3}{sin}^{2}\theta + \dfrac{2}{3}{cos}^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{9}{sin}^{2}\theta + \dfrac{4}{9}{cos}^{2}\theta + \dfrac{4}{9}sin\thetacos\theta$

$= \dfrac{1}{3}{sin}^{2}\theta + \dfrac{2}{3}{cos}^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{9}{sin}^{2}\theta + \dfrac{2}{9}{cos}^{2}\theta - \dfrac{4}{9}sin\thetacos\theta = 0$

$⇒ {sin}^{2}\theta + {cos}^{2}\theta - 2sin\thetacos\theta = 0$

$⇒ sin2\theta = 1$

$⇒ \theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}, n \in I$

$∴ A = \left\{\theta \in R: \theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}, n \in I\right\}$

52025.subject: Physics
52025.text: In a muonic atom, a muon of mass of $200$ times of that of electron and same charge is bound to the proton. The wavelengths of its Balmer series are in the range of
52025.sol:
A muon is an unstable elementary particle of mass nearly $200{m}_{e}$ and charge $\pm e$.

Here, a negative muon is given bound to a proton.

So, $m = 200{m}_{e}$ and $M = 1836{m}_{e}$

(as mass of a proton is $1836$ times of mass of electron)

So, reduced mass of system,

$m^{'} = \dfrac{mM}{m + M} = \dfrac{200{m}_{e} \times 1836{m}_{e}}{200{m}_{e} + 1836{m}_{e}} \approx 180{m}_{e}$

As mass of muon is comparable to mass of proton, we have to take account of motion of nucleus. That's way we are calculating reduced mass.

Now, as energy of an electron in $nth$ orbit is of $H$-atom,

${E}_{n} = \dfrac{me^{4}}{8{ε}_{0}^{2}h^{2}n^{2}}$

So, energy of a muon of muonic atom is

${E}_n^{'} = \dfrac{m^{'}e^{4}}{8{ε}_{0}^{2}h^{2}n^{2}} ⇒ {E}_n^{'} = 180{E}_{n}$

Now, considering a Balmer transition, $n = 3$ to $n = 2$.

$∴ \Delta E^{'} = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

or $\Delta E^{'} = {E}_{n = 3}^{'} - {E}_{n = 2}^{'} = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180\left({E}_{n = 3} - {E}_{n = 2}\right) = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180\left(\dfrac{- 13. 6}{32} - \dfrac{- 13. 6}{22}\right) = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180 \times 189eV = \dfrac{1240\left(eV \cdot nm\right)}{\lambda\left(nm\right)}$

$⇒ \lambda\left(nm\right) = 3. 6nm$

This emitted radiation is $X$-rays.

Note $X$-rays have a wavelength range of $0. 01nm$ to $10$ nm.

54881.subject: Chemistry
54881.text: Which from following statements is NOT true for phenol?
options: Pure phenol is odourless, nontoxic, high melting solid.
Boiling points of phenols increases with increase in molecular mass.
Phenols show appreciable solubility in water.
54881.sol:
Analyzing the properties of phenols:

A) Phenols are polar molecules: The hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) exhibits significant polarity due to electronegativity differences, resulting in a polar molecule. This statement is true.

B) Pure phenol is odourless, nontoxic, high melting solid: While phenol is a solid with a melting point near $40.5^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, it possesses a distinct carbolic odor and is both toxic and corrosive. Consequently, this statement is not true.

C) Boiling points of phenols increase with molecular mass: Enhanced van der Waals interactions with greater mass elevate boiling points, a trend consistent across organic compounds including phenols. This statement is true.

D) Phenols show appreciable solubility in water: Hydrogen bonding capability with water via the hydroxyl group facilitates solubility, exemplified by phenol's moderate solubility ($\approx 8.3 \text{ g}/100 \text{ mL}$ at $20^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$). This statement is true.

The statement not true is B.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

56457.subject: Chemistry
56457.text: What is the number of moles of silver chloride precipitated when excess silver nitrate is treated with one mole of pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride?
56457.sol:
Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride features a $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ center coordinated to five neutral $\mathrm{NH_3}$ ligands and one $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ ligand, giving the complex ion $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)5CO3}]^+$ with charge $+3 + 0 - 2 = +1$.

Silver nitrate test for ionic chloride: Each formula unit contains one $\mathrm{Cl-}$ ion, producing one mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitate per mole of compound.

$E = \frac{\text{mass of AgCl}}{\text{molar mass of AgCl}} = \frac{2.87\,\text{g}}{143.32\,\text{g/mol}} = 0.02\,\text{mol}$

Since one mole of compound yields one mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, the moles of silver chloride precipitated are $\mathbf{0.02\,\text{mol}}$.

57753.subject: Chemistry
57753.text: Which of the following alkyl chlorides on Wurtz reaction gives 2, 2, 5, 5- tetramethylhexane ?
57753.sol:
Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

$2\text{R-Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaCl}$

The given product is 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. Its structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$.

Cleaving the molecule symmetrically at the central $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond gives two identical alkyl groups, which are neopentyl groups, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-$.

Therefore, the required alkyl chloride is neopentyl chloride, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$

57905.subject: Chemistry
57905.text: The reactions of alkanes are explosive with which halogen?
57905.sol:
The reaction of alkanes with fluorine is difficult to control bacause the activation energy for hydrogen abstraction is so low.
The initiation step involves the homolytic cleavage of the $F - F$ bond.
$F - F \to \overset{.}{F} + \overset{.}{F} ; {E}_{a} = + 155kJ / mol$
This is a high activation energy. But only a few $F$ atoms need to form.
Each $F$ atom can then initiate thousands of propagation steps.
$C{H}_{4} + \overset{.}{F} \to C{H}_{3} F + \overset{.}{H}$
These steps are highly exothermic; $\Delta H^{o} = - 431kJ / mol.$

59092.text: A solution of non volatile solute has boiling point elevation $0.70$ K if $K_b$ for the solvent is $2.44\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$. What is the molality of the solution?
59092.sol:
The elevation in boiling point is given by the formula:

$\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$

where $\Delta T_b$ is the boiling point elevation, $K_b$ is the ebullioscopic constant, and $m$ is the molality of the solution.

Given:
$\Delta T_b = 0.70$ K
$K_b = 2.44$ K kg mol^{-1}$

Substituting the given values into the formula:

0.70 = 2.44 \times m$

$m = \dfrac{0.70}{2.44}$

$m \approx 0.286$ m

Answer: $0.286$ m

59160.subject: Chemistry
59160.text: Calculate the relative lowering of vapour pressure of solution containing 0.56 g nonvolatile solute in 100 g water [ molar mass of solute $=60 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ]
59160.sol:
The relative lowering of vapour pressure is given by Raoult's law, $\frac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = X_{\text{solute}} = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solute}} + n_{\text{solvent}}}$.

For a solute mass of $0.56 \text{g}$ with molar mass $60 \text{g} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}$, $n_{\text{solute}} = \frac{0.56}{60} = 0.009333 \text{mol}$.

For water as solvent with mass $100 \text{g}$ and molar mass $18 \text{g} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}$, $n_{\text{solvent}} = \frac{100}{18} = 5.5556 \text{mol}$.

The mole fraction is then $X_{\text{solute}} = \frac{0.009333}{0.009333 + 5.5556} = \frac{0.009333}{5.564933} \approx 0.0017$.

The relative lowering of vapour pressure is 0.0017, confirming option B.

61662.subject: Mathematics
61662.text: If $e^y + xy = e$, then the ordered pair $\left(\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}, \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2}\right)$ at $x = 0$ is equal to
61662.sol:
Given equation is $e^y + xy = e$.

Substituting $x = 0$ in the given equation:
$e^y + 0 = e \Rightarrow y = 1$

Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x$:
$e^y \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + y + x \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} = 0$

Substituting $x = 0 and y = 1$:
$e^1 \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 1 + 0 = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} = \dfrac{-1}{e}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:
$e^y \left(\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right)^2 + e^y \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} + \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = 0$

$e^y \left(\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right)^2 + 2\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + (e^y + x) \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = 0$

Substituting $x = 0$, $y = 1$, and $\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} = \dfrac{-1}{e}$:
$e \left(\dfrac{-1}{e}\right)^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{-1}{e}\right) + (e + 0) \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{e} - \dfrac{2}{e} + e \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = 0$

$-\dfrac{1}{e} + e \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2} = \dfrac{1}{e^2}$

Therefore, the ordered pair $\left(\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}, \dfrac{\text{d}^2 y}{\text{d}x^2}\right)$ is $\left(\dfrac{-1}{e}, \dfrac{1}{e^2}\right)$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{-1}{e}, \dfrac{1}{e^2}\right)$

64834.subject: Mathematics
64834.text:
If $0 \leqslant x \leqslant \pi$ and $81^{\sin ^2 x}+81^{\cos ^2 x}=30$
Then $x$ takes the value
64834.sol:
Given the equation $81^{\sin^2 x} + 81^{\cos^2 x} = 30$ with domain $0 \leqslant x \leqslant \pi$.

Using the identity $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$, substitute $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$ to rewrite the equation as $81^{\sin^2 x} + 81^{1 - \sin^2 x} = 30$.

Apply exponent rules to express it as $y + \frac{81}{y} = 30$, where $y = 81^{\sin^2 x}$ and $y > 0$.

Multiply through by $y$ to form the quadratic equation $y^2 - 30y + 81 = 0$, which factors as $(y - 3)(y - 27) = 0$, yielding $y = 3$ or $y = 27$.

For $y = 3$, $81^{\sin^2 x} = 3$. Since $81 = 3^4$, this becomes $3^{4\sin^2 x} = 3^1$, so $4\sin^2 x = 1$ and $\sin^2 x = \frac{1}{4}$.
In the domain, $\sin x \geqslant 0$, so $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$, giving $x = \frac{\pi}{6}$ or $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.

For $y = 27$, $81^{\sin^2 x} = 27$. Write $81 = 3^4$ and $27 = 3^3$ to get $3^{4\sin^2 x} = 3^3$, so $4\sin^2 x = 3$ and $\sin^2 x = \frac{3}{4}$.
With $\sin x \geqslant 0$, $\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, giving $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ or $x = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.

The solutions are thus $x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{6}$.

Comparing with the options, only Option A ($\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}$) contains valid solutions.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

65134.text: ABCD is a quadrilateral with $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}=\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{AD}}=\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{AC}}=2 \bar{a}+3 \overline{\mathrm{ b}}$. If its area is $\alpha$ times the area of the parallelogram with $\mathrm{AB}, \mathrm{AD}$ as adjacent sides, then the value of $\alpha$ is
65134.sol:
Define $\mathrm{AB} = \mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{AD} = \mathrm{b}$. The area of the parallelogram formed by these vectors is $A_{parallelogram} = |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}|$.
The quadrilateral ABCD is divided by diagonal $\mathrm{AC} = 2\mathrm{a} + 3\mathrm{b}$ into two triangles: $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$.
The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $\frac{1}{2} |\mathrm{a} \times (2\mathrm{a} + 3\mathrm{b})| = \frac{1}{2} |3(\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b})| = \frac{3}{2} |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}|$, as $\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{a} = \mathrm{0}$.
The area of $\triangle ADC$ is $\frac{1}{2} |\mathrm{b} \times (2\mathrm{a} + 3\mathrm{b})| = \frac{1}{2} |2(\mathrm{b} \times \mathrm{a})| = \frac{1}{2} | -2(\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}) | = |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}|$, using $\mathrm{b} \times \mathrm{b} = \mathrm{0}$ and $\mathrm{b} \times \mathrm{a} = -(\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b})$.
Summing these gives the total area: $\frac{3}{2} |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}| + |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}| = \frac{5}{2} |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}|$.
Given that this equals $\alpha \times |\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}|$, it follows that $\alpha = \frac{5}{2}$.
The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

66356.text: If only $5 \%$ of the total current is to be passed through galvanometer of resistance G, then the resistance of the shunt will be
66356.sol:
A galvanometer with internal resistance $G$ is converted into an ammeter by connecting a shunt resistance $S$ in parallel, allowing a total current $I$ to flow, of which only $I_g = 0.05I$ passes through the galvanometer.

The remaining current through the shunt is $I_s = I - I_g = 0.95I$.

Since the galvanometer and shunt are in parallel, the voltage across them is equal:

$I_g G = I_s S$

Substituting the known current ratios:

$0.05I \cdot G = 0.95I \cdot S$

Canceling the common factor of $I$:

$0.05G = 0.95S$

Solving for $S$:

$S = \frac{0.05G}{0.95} = \frac{G}{19}$

The shunt resistance must be $\frac{G}{19}$, matching option C.

66541.text: The kinetic energy of a free electron increases to 3 times the previous K.E. The ratio of new de-Broglie wavelength to previous de-Broglie wavelength is
66541.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$

where $K$ is the kinetic energy of the electron.

From the relation, $\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$

Given that the new kinetic energy $K_2 = 3K_1$.

The ratio of the new de-Broglie wavelength to the previous de-Broglie wavelength is

$\dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_1}{K_2}}$

$\dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_1}{3K_1}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$E_1 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_1} - \phi$

Given $\lambda_1 = 1.5\lambda_2 = \dfrac{3}{2}\lambda_2$, we can write:

From the second equation, $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_2} = E_2 + \phi$. Substituting this into the equation for $E_1$:

$E_1 = \dfrac{2}{3}(E_2 + \phi) - \phi$

$E_1 = \dfrac{2}{3}E_2 - \dfrac{1}{3}\phi$

Since the work function $\phi > 0$, it follows that:

$E_1 < \dfrac{2}{3}E_2$

Answer: $E_1 < 2E_2/3$

67006.subject: Physics
67006.text: Select the WRONG statement about polar molecules.
options: Polar molecules have permanent dipole moment.
A molecule in which centre of mass of positive charges does not coincide with the centre of mass of negative charges is a polar molecule.
Polar molecules act as tiny electric dipoles.
67006.sol:
In a polar molecule, the centre of mass of positive charges does not coincide with the centre of mass of negative charges. This separation of charges results in a permanent electric dipole moment, causing the molecule to act as a tiny electric dipole.

Because the charge distribution is uneven, polar molecules generally have an asymmetrical shape. Symmetrical molecules (like $\text{CO}_2$ or $\text{CH}_4$) have their centres of positive and negative charges coinciding, resulting in a net zero dipole moment, making them non-polar.

Therefore, the statement that polar molecules have a symmetrical shape is incorrect.

Answer: Polar molecules have symmetrical shape.

68681.text: A simple pendulum oscillates with an angular amplitude $\theta$. If the maximum tension in the string is twice the minimum tension then $\theta$ is
68681.sol:
Let the mass of the bob be $m$ and the length of the string be $l$.

At any angle $\phi$, the tension $T$ in the string is given by:

$T - mg \cos \phi = \dfrac{mv^2}{l}$

By conservation of energy, the velocity $v$ at angle $\phi$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = mg l (\cos \phi - \cos \theta)$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{mv^2}{l} = 2mg (\cos \phi - \cos \theta)$

Substituting this into the tension equation, we get:

$T = mg \cos \phi + 2mg (\cos \phi - \cos \theta) = mg (3 \cos \phi - 2 \cos \theta)$

The maximum tension occurs at the lowest point ($\phi = 0$):

$T_{\max} = mg (3 - 2 \cos \theta)$

The minimum tension occurs at the extreme positions ($\phi = \theta$):

$T_{\min} = mg (3 \cos \theta - 2 \cos \theta) = mg \cos \theta$

Given that $T_{\max} = 2 T_{\min}$:

$mg (3 - 2 \cos \theta) = 2 mg \cos \theta$

$3 - 2 \cos \theta = 2 \cos \theta$

$4 \cos \theta = 3$

$\cos \theta = 0.75$

$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.75)$

Answer: $\cos^{-1}(0.75)$

69181.text: A thin wire of length ' $L$ ' and uniform linear mass density ' $\lambda$ ' is bent into a circular ring. The moment of inertia of ring about a tangential axis in its plane is
69181.sol:
Given a wire of length $L$ with uniform linear mass density $\lambda$, the total mass is $M = \lambda L$.

When formed into a circular ring, the circumference equals the wire length, so $L = 2\pi R$ and $R = \frac{L}{2\pi}$.

The moment of inertia about a diameter is $I_d = \frac{MR^2}{2}$ by the perpendicular axis theorem.

Applying the parallel axis theorem for a tangential axis in the plane, located distance $R$ from the center:

$I_{\text{tangential}} = I_d + MR^2 = \frac{MR^2}{2} + MR^2 = \frac{3}{2}MR^2$.

Substituting $M = \lambda L$ and $R = \frac{L}{2\pi}$:

$I_{\text{tangential}} = \frac{3}{2}(\lambda L)\left(\frac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \frac{3\lambda L^3}{8\pi^2}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

69428.subject: Physics
69428.text: In common emitter amplifier, a change of $0.2$ mA in the base current causes a change of $5$ mA in the collector current. If input resistance is $2$ k$\Omega$ and voltage gain is $75$, the load resistance used in the circuit is
69428.sol:
The current gain $\beta$ in a common emitter amplifier is given by:

$\beta = \dfrac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B}$

Substituting the given values:

$\beta = \dfrac{5 \text{ mA}}{0.2 \text{ mA}} = 25$

The voltage gain $A_v$ is related to the current gain, load resistance $R_L$, and input resistance $R_{in}$ by the formula:

$A_v = \beta \times \dfrac{R_L}{R_{in}}$

Substituting the known values into the equation:

$75 = 25 \times \dfrac{R_L}{2 \text{ k}\Omega}$

$\dfrac{R_L}{2 \text{ k}\Omega} = \dfrac{75}{25} = 3$

$R_L = 3 \times 2 \text{ k}\Omega = 6 \text{ k}\Omega$

Answer: $6$ k$\Omega$

69833.text: Three black discs $x, y, z$ have radii $1 \mathrm{ m}, 2 \mathrm{ m}$ and $3 \mathrm{ m}$ respectively. The wavelength corresponding to maximum intensity are $200 \mathrm{ nm}$, $300 \mathrm{ nm}$ and $400 \mathrm{ nm}$ respectively. The relation between emissive power $E_x, E_y$ and $E_z$ is
69833.sol:
According to the Stefan's Law:
$\begin{aligned}
& E=\frac{\sigma A T^4}{A} \\
& \Rightarrow E \propto T^4
\end{aligned}$
According to the Wein's Law:
$\begin{aligned}
& T=\frac{k}{\lambda_m} \\
& \therefore E \propto \frac{A}{\lambda^4} \\
& E_x: E_y: E_z=\frac{1}{\lambda_x^4}: \frac{1}{\lambda^4}: \frac{1}{\lambda^4}=\frac{1}{200^4}: \frac{1}{300^4}: \frac{1}{400^4}
\end{aligned}$
The relation between emissive power $E_x, E_y and E_z$ is as follows:
$E x > E y > E z$

69908.text: A rigid diatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\right)$ is compressed adiabatically to volume $\left(\dfrac{V_i}{32}\right)$, where $V_i$ is the initial volume. The initial temperature of the gas is '$T_i$' K and the final temperature is '$x\,T_i$' K. The value of $x$ is
69908.sol:
For an adiabatic process, the relation between temperature and volume is given by $T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$.

$T_i V_i^{\gamma - 1} = T_f V_f^{\gamma - 1}$

$T_f = T_i \left(\dfrac{V_i}{V_f}\right)^{\gamma - 1}$

Given $\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}$ and $V_f = \dfrac{V_i}{32}$.

$T_f = T_i (32)^{\dfrac{7}{5} - 1}$

$T_f = T_i (2^5)^{\dfrac{2}{5}}$

$T_f = T_i (2^2) = 4 T_i$

Comparing with $T_f = x T_i$, we get $x = 4$.

Answer: $4$

69931.subject: Physics
69931.text: An insulated container contains a monoatomic gas of molar mass 'm'. The container is moving with velocity 'V'. If it is stopped suddenly, the change in temperature of the gas is (R-gas constant)
69931.sol:
Let the number of moles of the gas be $n$.

Total mass of the gas is $M = nm$.

The initial kinetic energy of the gas due to the motion of the container is $K = \dfrac{1}{2} M v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} nm v^2$.

When the container is suddenly stopped, this kinetic energy is completely converted into the internal energy of the gas since the container is insulated.

Change in internal energy is $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

For a monoatomic gas, $C_v = \dfrac{3}{2} R$.

Equating the kinetic energy to the change in internal energy:

$\dfrac{1}{2} nm v^2 = n \left(\dfrac{3}{2} R\right) \Delta T$

$\Delta T = \dfrac{mv^2}{3R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{mv^2}{3R}$

69989.text: Two gases A and B having same initial state (P, V, n, T). Now gas A is compressed to $\frac{\mathrm{V}}{8}$ by isothermal process and other gas $B$ is compressed to $\frac{V}{8}$ by adiabatic process. The ratio of final pressure of gas A and B is (Both gases are monoatomic, $\gamma=5 / 3$ )
69989.sol:
For isothermal process (gas A)
$\begin{aligned}
& P_1 V_1=P_2 V_2 \\
\therefore \quad & P_0\left(8 V_0\right)=P_2\left(V_0\right) \\
\Rightarrow & \Rightarrow P_2=8 P_0
\end{aligned}$For adiabatic process (gas B)
$\begin{aligned}
& P^\gamma=\text{ constant } \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{P_2}{P_1}=(8)^\gamma \\
\therefore \quad & P_2=(8)^\gamma P_0
\end{aligned}$Hence, $\frac{\left(\mathrm{P}_2\right)_{\mathrm{B}}}{\left(\mathrm{P}_1\right)_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{(8)^\gamma \mathrm{P}_0}{8 \mathrm{P}_0}=(8)^{\gamma-1}\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\left(P_2\right)_B}{\left(P_1\right)_A}=8^{2 / 3} \\
& =\sqrt[3]{64}=4 \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\left(P_1\right)_A}{\left(P_2\right)_B}=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}\ldots(\text{ given }, \gamma=5 / 3)$

71069.subject: Biology
71069.text: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation of ecological pyramids?
options: The base of each pyramid represents the first trophic level.
It does not accommodate a food-web.
Saprophytes are not given any place.
A given species may occupy more than one trophic level.
71069.sol:
The base of each pyramid represents the producers or the first trophic level. This is a fundamental characteristic of ecological pyramids, not a limitation.

The limitations of ecological pyramids include:
1. They do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.
2. They assume a simple food chain and do not accommodate a food web.
3. Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids despite their vital role in the ecosystem.

Answer: The base of each pyramid represents the first trophic level.

71103.subject: Biology
71103.text:
Match List I with List II
List I (Types of isolating mechanisms.)List II (Reason)
(A). Habitat isolation(I). Difference in the structure of reproductive organs
(B). Temporal isolation(II). Occupies different habitats and do not mate
(C). Ethological isolation(III). Mature sexually at different times
(D). Mechanical isolation(IV). Specific mating behavoiur of members
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71103.sol:
Habitat isolation occurs when two species occupy different habitats within the same area and thus rarely encounter each other to mate. Therefore, (A) matches (II).

Temporal isolation occurs when species breed or mature sexually at different times, such as different times of the day, different seasons, or different years. Therefore, (B) matches (III).

Ethological (behavioral) isolation is due to specific mating behaviors or courtship rituals that are unique to a species, preventing members of different species from mating. Therefore, (C) matches (IV).

Mechanical isolation happens when morphological differences, such as differences in the structure of reproductive organs, prevent successful mating. Therefore, (D) matches (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)

71658.subject: Chemistry
71658.text: What is the number of stereo structure of glucose?
71658.sol:
The open-chain structure of glucose is an aldohexose with the chemical formula $CHO-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH$.

In this structure, there are $4$ chiral carbon atoms (the four $CHOH$ groups).

Since the molecule is unsymmetrical (the two terminal groups are different, $CHO$ and $CH_2OH$), the total number of stereoisomers is given by the formula $2^n$, where $n$ is the number of chiral centers.

Substituting $n = 4$, we get $2^4 = 16$.

Thus, there are $16$ possible stereo structures for an aldohexose like glucose.

Answer: $16$

72118.subject: Physics
72118.text: In an ideal LC circuit, if the energy stored in the inductor is equal to energy stored in a capacitor, then the magnitude of charge Q stored in capacitor is (Q_0$ is the maximum charge)$
72118.sol:
Total energy in an ideal LC circuit is conserved and is equal to the maximum energy stored in the capacitor.

$E_{total} = \dfrac{Q_0^2}{2C}$

At any instant, the total energy is the sum of the energy stored in the capacitor (U_C$) and the inductor (U_L$).

$E_{total} = U_C + U_L$

Given that the energy stored in the inductor is equal to the energy stored in the capacitor (U_L = U_C$):

$E_{total} = 2U_C$

Substituting the expressions for energy:

\dfrac{Q_0^2}{2C} = 2 \left( \dfrac{Q^2}{2C} \right)

$Q^2 = $\dfrac{Q_0^2}{2}$

$Q = \dfrac{Q_0}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Q_0}{\sqrt{2}}$

72418.subject: Physics
72418.text:
The work done by an ideal gas during closed cycle 1\rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 1$ as shown in figure is
$
72418.sol:
The total work done by the gas is the algebraic sum of the work done in the two separate loops shown in the $P-V$ diagram.

From the indicated arrows, the lower loop is traversed in a clockwise direction. Thus, the work done in this loop is positive and equal to the area of the lower triangle.

$W_1 = +\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = +\dfrac{1}{2} \times (5V_0 - V_0) \times (3P_0 - P_0)$

$W_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4V_0 \times 2P_0 = 4P_0V_0$

The upper loop is traversed in a counter-clockwise direction. Thus, the work done in this loop is negative and equal to the negative of the area of the upper triangle.

The upper and lower triangles are similar because their bases are parallel. The ratio of their heights is $\dfrac{4P_0 - 3P_0}{3P_0 - P_0} = \dfrac{P_0}{2P_0} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Therefore, the base of the upper triangle is half the base of the lower triangle, which is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4V_0 = 2V_0$.

$W_2 = -\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2V_0 \times (4P_0 - 3P_0)$

$W_2 = -\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2V_0 \times P_0 = -P_0V_0$

The net work done during the complete cycle is $W = W_1 + W_2 = 4P_0V_0 - P_0V_0 = 3P_0V_0$.

72433.subject: Physics
72433.text: Thermodynamic change in the system from state $(P_1, V_1)$ to $(P_2, V_2)$ is shown in the figure. The work done by the system is
72433.sol:
The work done by the system during a thermodynamic process is equal to the area under the $P-V$ graph projected on the volume axis.

From the given graph, the process from state A to state D forms a trapezium with the volume axis.

The initial state A has coordinates $P_1 = 1 \times 10^5\ \text{N/m}^2$ and $V_1 = 1\ \text{m}^3$.

The final state D has coordinates $P_2 = 3 \times 10^5\ \text{N/m}^2$ and $V_2 = 5\ \text{m}^3$.

The work done $W$ is the area of this trapezium:

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} (P_1 + P_2) (V_2 - V_1)$

Substituting the values:

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} (1 \times 10^5 + 3 \times 10^5) (5 - 1)$

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} (4 \times 10^5) (4)$

$W = 2 \times 10^5 \times 4$

$W = 8 \times 10^5\ \text{J}$

Answer: $8 \times 10^5\ \text{J}$

I do not wish to suggest that because we were one nation we had no differences, but it is submitted that our leading men travelled throughout India either on foot or in bullock-carts. You will admit they were no fools. They knew that worship of God could have been performed just as well at home. They taught us that those whose hearts were aglow with righteousness had the Ganges in their own homes. But they saw that India was one undivided land so made by nature. They, therefore, argued that it must be one nation. The paragraph is written in a

73965.text: A ball of 0.1 kg mass is dropped on a hard floor from a height of 0.45 m and rises to a height of 0.20 m. If it was in touch with the floor for 0.1 s , the net force it applied on the floor while bouncing is: (take the gravitational acceleration $g=10 \mathrm{ m} \mathrm{ s}^{-2}$ )

\Rightarrow \quad u & =\sqrt{2 g h} \\
& =\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.45} \\
& =\sqrt{9}=3 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
After rebound some of its kinetic energy gets lost and remaining gets converted into Potential energy
Hence, $\quad \frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h^{\prime}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad v & =\sqrt{2 g h^{\prime}} \\
& =\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.20} \\
& =\sqrt{4}=2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
We know that, $\mathrm{F}=\frac{m v-m u}{t}=\frac{m(v-u)}{t}$
Taking sign consideration
$\mathrm{F}=\frac{0.1(-2-3)}{0.1}=-5 \mathrm{ N} .$
(-ve sign indicated retarding force)

76372.subject: Mathematics
76372.text:
Passage: Let $S$ and $T$ be the sets where $f(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{5x^2}{2}+6x+7$ decreases and increases respectively.

Question: What is $S$ equal to ?
76372.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - \dfrac{5x^2}{2} + 6x + 7$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6$

$f'(x) = (x - 2)(x - 3)$

For the function to be decreasing, $f'(x) \leq 0$.

$(x - 2)(x - 3) \leq 0$

$x \in [2,3]$

Therefore, the set $S$ where $f(x)$ decreases is $[2,3]$.

Answer: $[2,3]$

76580.text: What is the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the expansion of $\left(1-x^2\right)^{20}\left(2-x^2-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^{-5}$ ?
76580.sol:
$\left(1-x^2\right)^{20}\left[-\left(\frac{1}{x^2}+x^2-2\right)\right]^{-5}\begin{aligned}
& =-\left(1-x^2\right)^{20}\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)^{-10} \\

$\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)}=\int \frac{\mathrm{x}^6}{\mathrm{x}^7\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)} \cdot \mathrm{dx}$
Let $\mathrm{x}^7=\mathrm{t}\Rightarrow 7 x^6. d x=\mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow x^6 d x=\frac{d t}{7}$
Then $\int \frac{x^6 d x}{x^7\left(x^7+1\right)}=\frac{1}{7} \int \frac{d t}{t(t+1)}\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{7}\left[\int \frac{1}{t} \mathrm{dt}-\int \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}+1} \mathrm{dt}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{7}[\ln |\mathrm{t}|-\ln |\mathrm{t}+1|]+\mathrm{c} \\
& =\frac{1}{7} \ln \left|\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}+1}\right|+\mathrm{c} \\
& =\frac{1}{7} \ln \left|\frac{\mathrm{x}^7}{\mathrm{x}^7+1}\right|+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$

Amongst the following statements, select the set having statements which was proposed by Dalton.
(1) All the atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass. Atoms of different elements differ in mass.
(2) When gases combine or reproduced in a chemical reaction they do so in a simple ratio by volume provided all gases are at the same T & P

93713.text: A liquid drop having surface energy $E$ is spread into $512$ droplets of same size. The final surface energy of the droplets is
93713.sol:
The surface area of the liquid drop is $A = 4{\piR}^{2}$

Its surface energy is $E$

When the drop splits in $512$ droplets, the surface area of each droplet is $4{\pir}^{2}$

$∴$ Total surface area ${A}_{2}= 512 \times 4{\pir}^{2}$

The volume of bigger drop is $\dfrac{4}{3}{\piR}^{3}$ and volume of small droplets is $512 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pir}^{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{4}{3}{\piR}^{3} = 512 \times \dfrac{4}{3}{\pir}^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{8}$

$∴ {A}_{2} = 512 \times 4{\pir}^{2} = 512 \times 4\pi\left(\dfrac{R}{8}\right)2 = 8{A}_{1}$

Surface energy $E = A . T$ ($T$ is surface tension and $A$ is area)

$∴ \dfrac{En}{E0} = \dfrac{{A}_{2} ⋅ T}{{A}_{1} ⋅ T} = \dfrac{8 ⋅ {A}_{1}}{A1} = 8$

$∴ {E}_{n} = 8E$

96502.subject: Botany
96502.text:
Consider the following statements concerning food chains.

I. Removal of 80% tigers from an area resulted in greatly increased growth of vegetation.
II. In a grassland ecosystem with deers being primary consumers, removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers.
III. The length of food chains is generally limited to 3 to 4 trophic levels due to energy loss.
IV. The length of food chains may vary from 2 to 8 trophic levels.

Which two of the above statements are correct?
96502.sol: The series of organisms eating one and being eaten by other is called food chain. A simple food chain consists of producers, herbivores and carnivores. The length of food chain is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels due to energy loss. In grazing food chain, the producers (i.e., plants) are eaten by herbivores (i.e., rabbit, dear, cow, etc) and are eaten by carnivores. Therefore, the removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers.

96523.subject: Botany
96523.text:
Match the process of decomposition with the event that occurs in it:
&
$( i )$ Fragmentation $\left(A\right)$ Degradation of detritus by bacterial and fungal enzymes
$( ii )$ Leaching $\left(B\right)$ Precipitation of water-soluble nutrients as unavailable salt
$( iii )$ Catabolism $\left(C\right)$ Break down of detritus into smaller particles
96523.sol: Fragmentation, leaching, and catabolism are important steps of decomposition. Fragmentation is the process of breakdown of detritus, consisting of remains of dead plants and animals, into smaller particles by detrivores like an earthworm. The water-soluble inorganic nutrients obtained from the process of decomposition get precipitated as unavailable salts. This process is known as leaching. Degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacterial and fungal enzymes is called catabolism.

96927.subject: Botany
96927.text: Which of the following is incorrect pairing of plant and the characteristic?
options: Variation in the length of filaments within a flower: Salvia
Ovary is one-chambered but it becomes two chambered due to formation of a false septum: Argemone
The gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it: Guava
96927.sol: In the hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal. In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary. Hence, the ovary is said to be inferior as in flowers of guava and cucumber. There may be a variation in the length of filaments within a flower, as in Salvia and mustard. Flowers are termed syncarpous when carpels are fused, as in mustard and tomato. In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part. Ovary is one-chambered but it becomes twochambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and Argemone.

97088.subject: Botany
97088.text: Arrange the different parts of the root vertically, from the top to the bottom.
options: Region of elongation& → Root hair& → Region of maturation& → Region of meristematic activity& → Root cap
Region of maturation → Root hair → Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap
Region of maturation& →& Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity& → Root cap → Root hair
Root cap& →& Region of meristematic activity → Region of elongation& → Root hair& → Region of maturation
97088.sol:
The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap. It protects the tender apex of the root as it makes its way through the soil. A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly. The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length. This region is called the region of elongation. The cells of the elongation zone gradually differentiate and mature. Hence, this zone, proximal to region of elongation, is called the region of maturation. From this region some of the epidermal cells form very fine and delicate, thread-like structures called root hairs. These root hairs absorb water and minerals from the soil.

Vertically, from top to bottom, the order is:& Region of maturation →& Root hair →& Region of elongation → Region of meristematic activity → Root cap

100106.subject: Physics
100106.text:
Match List-I with List-II, where $h$, $c$, $k_B$, $\sigma_s$, $b$, and $T$ represent Planck's constant, speed of light, Boltzmann constant, Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Wien's displacement constant, and temperature, respectively.

List-IList-II
A. $\dfrac{h c}{k_B T}$I. $[\text{M}\text{L}^{-1}\text{T}^{-2}]$
B. $\dfrac{\sigma_s T^4}{c}$II. $[\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]$
C. $\dfrac{b k_B}{h}$III. $[\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]$
D. $\dfrac{\sigma_s b^4}{h c^2}$IV. $[\text{L}]$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
100106.sol:
Let us find the dimensional formula for each expression in List-I.

A. $\dfrac{h c}{k_B T}$ :
$[h c] = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-1}] \times [\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}] = [\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]$
$[k_B T] = \text{Energy} = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]$
$\left[\dfrac{h c}{k_B T}\right] = \dfrac{[\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]} = [\text{L}]$ (Matches IV)

B. $\dfrac{\sigma_s T^4}{c}$ :
$[\sigma_s T^4] = \text{Power per unit area} = \dfrac{[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-3}]}{[\text{L}^2]} = [\text{M}\text{T}^{-3}]$
$[c] = [\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]$
$\left[\dfrac{\sigma_s T^4}{c}\right] = \dfrac{[\text{M}\text{T}^{-3}]}{[\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]} = [\text{M}\text{L}^{-1}\text{T}^{-2}]$ (Matches I)

C. $\dfrac{b k_B}{h}$ :
$[b] = [\text{L}\text{K}]$
$[k_B] = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}]$
$[b k_B] = [\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]$
$[h] = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]$
$\left[\dfrac{b k_B}{h}\right] = \dfrac{[\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]} = [\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]$ (Matches II)

D. $\dfrac{\sigma_s b^4}{h c^2}$ :
$[\sigma_s] = [\text{M}\text{T}^{-3}\text{K}^{-4}]$
$[b^4] = [\text{L}^4\text{K}^4]$
$[\sigma_s b^4] = [\text{M}\text{L}^4\text{T}^{-3}]$
$[h c^2] = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-1}] \times [\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}] = [\text{M}\text{L}^4\text{T}^{-3}]$
$\left[\dfrac{\sigma_s b^4}{h c^2}\right] = \dfrac{[\text{M}\text{L}^4\text{T}^{-3}]}{[\text{M}\text{L}^4\text{T}^{-3}]} = [\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]$ (Matches III)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

100334.subject: Physics
100334.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a particle travels between two points with speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ ($v_1 \neq v_2$) for two equal time intervals, its average speed is strictly greater than if it travels with the same speeds for two equal distances.

Reason (R): The arithmetic mean of two distinct positive numbers is always greater than their harmonic mean.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
100334.sol:
For a particle travelling with speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ for two equal time intervals, the average speed is the arithmetic mean (AM):
$v_{avg, time} = \dfrac{v_1 + v_2}{2}$

For a particle travelling with the same speeds for two equal distances, the average speed is the harmonic mean (HM):
$v_{avg, dist} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$

By the mathematical property of positive distinct numbers, the arithmetic mean is strictly greater than the harmonic mean (AM > HM).
Therefore, $v_{avg, time} > v_{avg, dist}$.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

100895.subject: Physics
100895.text: The variation of force $F$ acting on a particle with its position $x$ is represented by a straight line graph. The force increases linearly from $10\text{ N}$ at $x = 0$ to $30\text{ N}$ at $x = 4\text{ m}$. The work done by the force in moving the particle from $x = 0$ to $x = 4\text{ m}$ is
100895.sol:
The work done by a variable force is equal to the area under the force-position ($F-x$) graph.

The given graph is a straight line from $(0, 10)$ to $(4, 30)$, which forms a trapezium with the $x$-axis.

The parallel sides of the trapezium are $F_1 = 10\text{ N}$ and $F_2 = 30\text{ N}$, and the perpendicular distance between them is $x = 4\text{ m}$.

$W = \text{Area of trapezium} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (F_1 + F_2) \times x$

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (10 + 30) \times 4$

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 40 \times 4 = 80\text{ J}$

Answer: $80\text{ J}$

102784.subject: Physics
102784.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The electric potential and the electric field intensity at the centre of a square having four fixed point charges at their vertices as shown in figure are zero.
Reason (R) : If electric potential at a point is zero then the magnitude of electric field at that point must be zero. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
102784.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. The electric potential is a scalar quantity, and at the center of the square, the potential due to the two positive charges cancels out the potential due to the two negative charges because they are equidistant from the center.
\(V=\frac{k(+q)}{r}+\frac{k(-q)}{r}+\frac{k(+q)}{r}+\frac{k(-q)}{r}=0\)
The electric field is a vector quantity. The electric field vectors from the two positive charges point away from them, towards the center, and the vectors from the two negative charges point towards them, away from the center. Due to the symmetry of the charge arrangement, the horizontal and vertical components of these vectors at the center cancel each other out, resulting in a net electric field of zero.
Reason (R) is false. The relationship between electric potential (\(V\)) and electric field (\(E\)) is given by \(E=-\nabla V\). This equation shows that the electric field is the negative gradient of the potential. A zero potential at a point does not necessarily mean the gradient is zero. A classic example is the midpoint of an electric dipole, where the potential is zero but the electric field is non-zero. The electric field is dependent on the change in potential with distance, not the absolute value of the potential.
The correct option is (3) (A) is true but (R) is false.

103795.sol: Let number of turns $=\mathrm{n}$ $\begin{aligned} & n \times 6 a=24 a \\ & \therefore \quad n=4 \\ & \end{aligned}$ Magnetic moment, $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{nIA}=$ 4IA $\begin{aligned} & \because \text{ Area$ of $hexagone }=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a}^2 \sin 60^{\circ}+\mathrm{a} \cdot 2 \mathrm{a} \sin 60^{\circ} \\ & \quad+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a}^2 \sin 120^{\circ}\end{aligned} =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2+\sqrt{3} a^2+\frac{\sqrt{3} a^2}{4}=\frac{6 \sqrt{3} a^2}{4}=\frac{3 \sqrt{3} a^2}{2}$ Hence, magnetic moment $=4 I\left(\frac{3 \sqrt{3} a^2}{2}\right)=6 \sqrt{3} a^2$

104083.subject: Physics
104083.text: The instantaneous current from an AC source is given by the equation $i = 14.14 \sin(100 \pi t)$, where $i$ is in amperes and $t$ is in seconds. What is the RMS value of the current?
104083.sol:
The standard equation for an alternating current is $i = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$, where $I_0$ is the peak current.

Comparing the given equation $i = 14.14 \sin(100 \pi t)$ with the standard form, we find the peak current to be:
$I_0 = 14.14\text{ A}$

The RMS value of the current ($I_{rms}$) is related to the peak current by the formula:
$I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$

Using the approximation $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, we get:
$I_{rms} = \dfrac{14.14}{1.414} = 10\text{ A}$

Therefore, the RMS value of the current is $10\text{ A}$.

Answer: $10\text{ A}$

104695.subject: Physics
104695.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through three polaroids where the first and third are crossed, the maximum possible transmitted intensity is $\dfrac{I_0}{4}$.

Reason (R): The transmitted intensity is maximum when the middle polaroid is placed at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with respect to the transmission axis of the first polaroid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
104695.sol:
When unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through the first polaroid, the transmitted intensity is $I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$.

Let the middle polaroid be at an angle $\theta$ with respect to the first. The third polaroid is crossed with the first, so its angle with the middle polaroid is $(90^{\circ} - \theta)$.

The final transmitted intensity is:
$I = I_1 \cos^2\theta \cos^2(90^{\circ} - \theta)$
$I = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2\theta \sin^2\theta = \dfrac{I_0}{8} \sin^2(2\theta)$

For maximum intensity, $\sin^2(2\theta) = 1$, which gives $2\theta = 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow \theta = 45^{\circ}$. Thus, the Reason is true.

Substituting $\theta = 45^{\circ}$, the maximum transmitted intensity is $I_{max} = \dfrac{I_0}{8}$. The Assertion states it is $\dfrac{I_0}{4}$, which is incorrect because it ignores the initial $50\%$ intensity drop for unpolarized light. Thus, the Assertion is false.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

105545.subject: Physics
105545.text: The graph showing the variation of stopping potential ($V_0$) with the reciprocal of the wavelength ($\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$) of the incident light for a photosensitive material has an $x$-intercept of $2.5 \times 10^6$ m$^{-1}$. Which of the following incident wavelengths will not give rise to the photoelectric effect?
105545.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation:
$eV_0 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

Rearranging for stopping potential $V_0$:
$V_0 = \dfrac{hc}{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\right) - \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$

The $x$-intercept of the $V_0$ versus $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$ graph occurs when the stopping potential $V_0 = 0$.
At this point, $\dfrac{hc}{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\right) = \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$, which means $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{\Phi}{hc}$.

This specific value of $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$ corresponds to the reciprocal of the threshold wavelength ($\dfrac{1}{\lambda_0}$).

Given the $x$-intercept is $2.5 \times 10^6$ m$^{-1}$:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda_0} = 2.5 \times 10^6$ m$^{-1}$

$\lambda_0 = \dfrac{1}{2.5 \times 10^6}$ m $= 0.4 \times 10^{-6}$ m $= 400$ nm

For the photoelectric effect to occur, the incident wavelength must be less than or equal to the threshold wavelength ($\lambda \le \lambda_0$).
Therefore, radiation will not produce photoelectrons if $\lambda > 400$ nm.

Among the given options, $500$ nm is greater than $400$ nm and will not give rise to the photoelectric effect.

Answer: $500$ nm

105577.subject: Physics
105577.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a photon-particle collision, the total energy and total momentum are conserved, but the number of photons may not be conserved.
Reason (R): During a collision with matter, a photon may be completely absorbed or a new photon may be created.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
105577.sol:
According to the photon picture of electromagnetic radiation, in any photon-particle collision (such as a photon-electron collision), the fundamental conservation laws of total energy and total momentum hold strictly true.

However, unlike classical particles, photons can be created or destroyed. During an interaction with matter, an existing photon may be completely absorbed by an electron, or a new photon may be emitted. Therefore, the total number of photons is not a conserved quantity.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains why the number of photons may not be conserved in Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

107745.subject: Chemistry
107745.text: Which of the following aromatic compounds contains exactly $15\ \sigma$ bonds and $4\ \pi$ bonds?
107745.sol:
The number of $\sigma$ bonds in a molecule containing one ring can be calculated as the total number of atoms in the molecule. Let us evaluate each option:

Benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5CHO$): Total atoms = $6 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 14$. Thus, it has $14\ \sigma$ bonds. It contains $3\ \pi$ bonds in the benzene ring and $1\ \pi$ bond in the carbonyl group, giving $4\ \pi$ bonds.

Toluene ($C_6H_5CH_3$): Total atoms = $6 + 5 + 1 + 3 = 15$. It has $15\ \sigma$ bonds. However, it only has $3\ \pi$ bonds (in the benzene ring).

Phenol ($C_6H_5OH$): Total atoms = $6 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 13$. It has $13\ \sigma$ bonds and $3\ \pi$ bonds.

Benzoic acid ($C_6H_5COOH$): Total atoms = $6 + 5 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 15$. It has $15\ \sigma$ bonds. It contains $3\ \pi$ bonds in the benzene ring and $1\ \pi$ bond in the carboxylic acid group ($-C=O$), giving a total of $4\ \pi$ bonds.

Therefore, benzoic acid is the compound that contains exactly $15\ \sigma$ bonds and $4\ \pi$ bonds.

Answer: Benzoic acid

109429.subject: Chemistry
109429.sol:
$\mathrm{NaNO}_3$ is salt formed by the combination of a strong acid $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ and a strong base $\mathrm{NaOH}$ and hence it is neutral with a $\mathrm{pH}$.
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOK}$ is formed by the combination of weak acid $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and strong base $\mathrm{KOH}$ and hence $\mathrm{pH}$ will be above 7 .
$\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ is formed by the formation of strong and $\mathrm{HCl}$ and a weak base $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and hence $\mathrm{pH}$ will be lesser than 7.
$\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ is a salt formed by the strong base $\mathrm{NaOH}$ and weak acid $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$. Hence, $\mathrm{pH}$ of the salt will be highest.
The pH scale was invented in 1909 by a Danish biochemist Soren Sorensen. It describes how many hydrogen ions (protons) are present in a solution: the higher the pH, the lower the hydrogen ion concentration, and vice versa. But the scale does not have fixed limits, so it is indeed possible to have a pH above 14 or below zero. For example, concentrated hydrochloric acid can have a pH of around -1 , while sodium hydroxide solution can have a pH as high as 15 .

111009.text:
Identify correct statements from the following:
i. \(\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3\) is a monobasic acid.
ii. The correct formula of borax is \(\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{~B}_4 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{OH})_3\right] 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\).
iii. \(\mathrm{NaBH}_4\) is a reducing agent.
111009.sol:
The explanations of given statements are as follows : (i) \($\mathrm{H}}_{3} \mathrm{BO}$}_{3}\) is a monobasic acid because in aqueous solution, it coordinates with a molecule of water to form a hydrated species,
\(\mathrm{B}^{3+}\) ion pulls the \($\sigma$\)-electron charge of coordinated \($\mathrm{O}$\)-atom towards itself. The coordinated oxygen, in turn, pull the \($\sigma$\)-electrons of \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond of the attached water molecule towards itself. This facilitates the removal of \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\)ion from the \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond. It can be written as follows: \($\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_$3+$\mathrm{H}}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_4 \Gamma+\mathrm{H}^{+}\right.\) (ii) The correct formula for borax is \(\mathrm{Na}$}_{2}$\left[\mathrm{~B}}_{4} \mathrm{O}$}_{7}\right] $\cdot$10 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}$\). (iii) \(\mathrm{NaBH}$}_{4}\) is a selective reducing agent for aldehydes, ketones and ester. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) are correct.

Match List-I with List-II

  List-I
(Mixture)		   List-II
(Purification Process)
A Chloroform & Aniline I Steam distillation
B Benzoic acid & Napthalene II Sublimation
C Water & Aniline III Distillation
D Napthalene & Sodium chloride IV Crystallisation
options: $A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II$
$A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II$
$A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I$
$A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II$
111714.sol:
(A) Chloroform $+$ Aniline $\to$ $III$ Distillation

(B) Benzoic acid $+$ Napthalene $\to IV$ Crystallisation

(C) Water $+$ Aniline $\to I$ Steam distillation

(D) Napthalene $+$ Sodium chloride $\to II$ Sublimation

Aniline is purified using the process of steam distillation because aniline is steam volatile and it is insoluble in water.

Chloroform and aniline having boiling points $334K$ and $457K$ can be separated by distillation. More volatile chloroform vaporizes first and is collected in the receiver. Aniline is left in the distillation flask.

Benzoic acid is soluble in hot water but naphthalene is not soluble, hence separation can be carried out by hot water crystallisation.

Naphthalene can also be separated by sublimation from non-volatile at room temperature.

The vapor of naphthalene can be collected and solidified.

116349.subject: Chemistry
116349.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the synthesis of ammonia via Haber's process:

Statement I: $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3$ moles of $H_{2}$ to give $2$ moles of $NH_{3}$.
Statement II: $22.4$ L of $N_{2}$ at STP reacts completely with $67.2$ L of $H_{2}$ at STP to give $44.8$ L of $NH_{3}$.
Statement III: $28$ g of $N_{2}$ reacts completely with $6$ g of $H_{2}$ to give $34$ g of $NH_{3}$.
Statement IV: If equal masses of $N_{2}$ and $H_{2}$ are taken, $N_{2}$ will act as the limiting reagent.

How many of the above statements are correct?
116349.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for Haber's process is:
$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_{3}(g)$

Statement I is correct as the stoichiometric coefficients directly give the molar ratio: $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3$ moles of $H_{2}$ to produce $2$ moles of $NH_{3}$.

Statement II is correct because at STP, $1$ mole of any ideal gas occupies $22.4$ L. Thus, $1 \times 22.4$ L of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3 \times 22.4$ L ($67.2$ L) of $H_{2}$ to yield $2 \times 22.4$ L ($44.8$ L) of $NH_{3}$.

Statement III is correct as the molar mass of $N_{2}$ is $28$ g/mol, $H_{2}$ is $2$ g/mol, and $NH_{3}$ is $17$ g/mol. Therefore, $28$ g of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3 \times 2$ g ($6$ g) of $H_{2}$ to produce $2 \times 17$ g ($34$ g) of $NH_{3}$.

Statement IV is correct. If we take equal masses (e.g., $28$ g of each), we have $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ and $14$ moles of $H_{2}$. Since $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ requires only $3$ moles of $H_{2}$, $H_{2}$ is in excess and $N_{2}$ is the limiting reagent.

All four statements are correct.

Answer: $4$
